reader.where: Set up each repo once, line 168: "belongs in your own `CLAUDE.md`, which every Skill reads."
reader.problem: Skills don't read CLAUDE.md. The agent loads it at the start of every session, which is why a preference there applies whichever Skill is running. 'Which every Skill reads' gives a cold reader the wrong picture of the mechanism, which line 24 explained correctly ('a file of standing instructions the agent reads at the start of every session').
reader.evidence: Lesson line 24. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: CLAUDE.md files are instructions that "Claude reads ... at the start of every session". No 1.3.1 SKILL.md tells the agent to open CLAUDE.md. Setup only writes to it (setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md:74-82).
reader.fix: "... belongs in your own `CLAUDE.md`, which loads in every session." (+1 word)

reader.where: Set up each repo once, line 168: "commit them, and everyone who clones the repo (downloads a copy with Git) gets the same setup."
reader.problem: For a reader who barely uses Git, a commit (glossed at line 30 as 'a saved snapshot of your project in Git') stays on their own computer. A teammate cloning from GitHub gets the files only after they're pushed. A Visitor who commits but doesn't push will think the setup is shared when it isn't. The why-clone-needs-setup feedback ('Uncommitted, those files stayed on your computer') carries the same gap.
reader.evidence: Lesson line 30's commit gloss. grep finds no 'push' anywhere in the Lesson. The clone gloss at line 168 ('downloads a copy') implies a shared copy somewhere, but the Lesson never says how files get there.
reader.fix: "commit them and push them (send them to GitHub), and everyone who clones the repo (downloads a copy with Git) gets the same setup." (+6 words; if the budget is tight, leave this until the PR + ship Lesson covers pushing)

quiz.where: Checkpoint what-loads-early (lines 83-93) and Final test why-light-context (lines 461-471)
quiz.problem: The Final test question re-asks the Checkpoint's fact (only name and description load until a Skill runs) with mirrored distractors. quiz.evidence: Checkpoint a 'All of it' maps to Final test b 'They load in full'. Checkpoint c 'Nothing at all until you type its name' maps to Final test c 'never touch the context window' and d 'Only Skills you type ever load'. Checkpoint right b 'Only its name and its two-line description' maps to Final test right a 'Until one runs, a Skill adds a line'. Writing guide, Questions: 'Don't reuse a Checkpoint as a Final test question.' (The round-2 decline was about rewording the right option, not about this overlap.)
quiz.fix:
Keep the id and test the flag's context cost (goals 1 and 2) instead. The right answer stays at a:
```test why-light-context
A friend is writing ten Skills of her own. Each runs a long process she always starts herself, but she leaves out `disable-model-invocation: true` "to keep them flexible". What does that cost her?
- [x] Ten descriptions sitting in every session, used or not.
  > Right. Without the flag, each description stays loaded so the agent can start the Skill itself. With it, a Skill she only types costs nothing until it runs.
- [ ] Nothing: no Skill touches the context window until it runs.
  > Model-invoked Skills keep their descriptions in the window from the start of each session, so the agent can spot a match.
- [ ] All ten bodies load at the start of every session.
  > A body loads only when its Skill runs. Before that, only the name and description are there.
- [ ] She can no longer start them by typing their names.
  > You can type any Skill's name. The flag only decides whether the agent can start it too.
```
Visible lengths are 55, 59, 50 and 51, so the right answer is neither the longest nor the shortest. The word count is about the same as now.
